content: Simvastatin is a medication prescribed to reduce the levels of cholesterol and certain other fatty substances in the blood. It is used in conjunction with lifestyle changes such as a healthy diet, weight loss, and regular exercise. Cholesterol is a fat-like substance that can accumulate along the walls of arteries, a condition known as atherosclerosis. This buildup can restrict blood flow and reduce the oxygen supply to vital organs like the heart and brain. By lowering cholesterol and fat levels in the blood, simvastatin helps decrease the risk of heart disease, angina (chest pain), strokes, and heart attacks. Simvastatin belongs to a class of drugs called HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, commonly known as statins. It works by slowing down the production of cholesterol in the body. In addition to taking simvastatin, adopting healthy daily habits, such as eating a diet low in saturated fat and cholesterol, exercising for at least 30 minutes on most days, and losing weight if overweight, can further help lower cholesterol levels. Simvastatin is available in tablet form and is taken orally, usually one to three times a day. It should be taken at the same time(s) each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take simvastatin exactly as directed, without increasing or decreasing the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it, but not more than once every four weeks. Continue taking simvastatin even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use for other conditions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking simvastatin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to simvastatin or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. Certain medications, such as erythromycin, HIV protease inhibitors (e.g., indinavir, ritonavir, saquinavir), nefazodone, other cholesterol-lowering drugs (e.g., fenofibrate, gemfibrozil, niacin), telithromycin, and verapamil, may interact with simvastatin. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have liver disease, as simvastatin is contraindicated in such cases. Also, let your doctor know if you consume large amounts of alcohol, have a history of liver or kidney disease, or are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking simvastatin, stop taking it immediately and contact your doctor. Do not breastfeed while on this medication. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking simvastatin. Additionally, ask your doctor about the safe use of alcohol while on this medication, as alcohol can increase the risk of serious side effects. Avoid consuming large quantities of grapefruit juice (more than one quart per day) while taking simvastatin, as it can interfere with the medication's effectiveness. Follow a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet, which includes foods like cottage cheese, fat-free milk, fish (not canned in oil), vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils and margarines (e.g., corn, safflower, canola, soybean oils). Avoid foods high in fat, such as fatty meats, liver, egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, shortening, lard, pastries, cakes, cookies, gravy, peanut butter, chocolate, olives, potato chips, coconut, cheese (other than cottage cheese), coconut oil, palm oil, and fried foods. If you miss a dose of simvastatin, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Simvastatin may cause side effects. Minor side effects include constipation. If you experience severe side effects, such as muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness; lack of energy; fever; yellowing of the skin or eyes; pain in the upper right part of the stomach; nausea; extreme tiredness; unusual bleeding or bruising; loss of appetite; flu-like symptoms; rash; hives; itching; difficulty breathing or swallowing; swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; or hoarseness, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store simvastatin in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order tests before and during treatment to monitor your response to simvastatin. Inform your doctor and laboratory personnel that you are taking simvastatin before undergoing any tests. Do not share your medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
